title: Legal Defense Plan for Human-in-the-Loop Workers
one_liner: A USCCA-style membership that protects the nurse, safety driver or loan officer who gets blamed when AI recommends and a human signs, plus an 'override receipt' log the member personally owns.
customer: Unions, state nurses' associations and professional societies (radiologic technologists, CRNAs, claims adjusters, AV teleoperators and safety drivers) as distribution partners. Members pay through a dues add-on, or employers buy it as a retention benefit.
problem: Regulations and enterprise policies demand 'meaningful human oversight', which in practice makes the human the liability sponge, the 'moral crumple zone'. Uber's Tempe safety driver was criminally charged, and nurse RaDonda Vaught was convicted after overriding an automated dispensing cabinet. Employer indemnities and malpractice policies rarely cover AI-specific disputes, licensing-board action, or retaliation for raising concerns.
solution: (1) A prepaid legal defense retainer covering civil, licensing-board and criminal matters, with panel counsel experienced in tech-mediated harm. (2) 'Override receipts': a light app or extension where the member logs each override, disagreement or safety concern, with hashed timestamps in a member-owned escrow. (3) Plain-English 'working with this AI tool' duty briefings per workplace system. (4) Aggregated, anonymised incident data that gives unions leverage in bargaining over staffing and AI use.
why_now: AI decision support is now standard in hospitals (sepsis alerts, ambient scribes) and in robotaxi remote operations. Human-oversight duties are being written into the EU AI Act and state laws. Insurers' AI exclusions signal to employers that AI losses may be uninsured, so risk will be pushed down to individual workers. Unions are actively bargaining over AI in 2025-26.
revenue_model: $9-19 per member per month through associations, with margin after panel counsel and a reinsurer or legal-plan administrator. Employer-paid group plans and individual upsells.
non_obvious_insight: The person who actually absorbs AI risk is neither the deployer nor the vendor but the individual signer, and no product exists for them. Unions already have distribution and every reason to buy. The override-receipt record may be worth more than the defense cover, because it is the human-oversight evidence courts will look for, and it hands the union data on unsafe deployments.
first_30_days: Pick one narrow group, such as AV teleoperators and safety drivers or nurses in one state. Get an MOU with one union local or association. Retain a defense-firm panel at group rates. Ship the override log as a Chrome extension or SMS bot. Pre-sell 300 members at $12 per month, and check state prepaid-legal-plan rules first.

title: Apprentice Athlete: Injury-Proofing the Skilled Trades
one_liner: An 8-week pre-apprenticeship that conditions and movement-screens new electricians, plumbers and pipefitters so they survive the first two years.
customer: Joint apprenticeship training centers (IBEW/NECA, UA, IEC, ABC), community-college trade programs, and the workers' comp carriers and brokers behind contractors. Contractors pay per placed apprentice.
problem: Electricians have about 72.7k openings a year (data-center demand) and plumbers about 42k, but the 4-5 year apprenticeship path is bottlenecked by employer sponsors and weak pre-apprenticeship screening. Overexertion and strain injuries are consistently a leading cause of lost-time injuries and feed early attrition. Many entrants are sedentary career-changers, including displaced white-collar grads (42% of recent grads are underemployed).
solution: 'Apprentice Athlete' runs 3 sessions a week for 8 weeks in existing gyms, taught by athletic trainers and strength coaches. It uses trade-specific drills (overhead conduit work, ladder and pipe carries, crawlspace mobility, grip endurance), phone-video or cheap-wearable movement screens, and an injury-prevention curriculum. Completion, not a fitness score, earns JATC pre-apprenticeship credit and can slot in as a short program eligible for Workforce Pell where approved. It is structured as training rather than a hiring screen, to stay clear of ADA limits.
why_now: Workforce Pell launched July 1, 2026 but only 5 programs are approved. Apprenticeship-linked programs get a fast lane, and up to 49% of instruction can be delivered by employers or unions. Data-center demand is pulling electricians, and AI-exposed grads are pivoting to trades. Phone pose-estimation and cheap wearables are now good enough to measure movement quality.
revenue_model: $400-800 per apprentice per cohort paid by contractor, JATC or Pell/WIOA funds. A $100-200k pilot contract with a comp carrier tied to premium credits. Then per-seat licensing to gyms and trainers who run the program (they keep 60-70%).
non_obvious_insight: The trades treat the body as a consumable, while sports treat it as an appreciating asset. Comp carriers already have loss runs showing injuries cluster in the first 24 months, so a $600 conditioning program pays back if it prevents one strain claim per few dozen apprentices. Trade schools cannot have that ROI conversation, but insurers can.
first_30_days: Partner with one IEC/ABC chapter or a community-college trades program. Run a 6-week pilot for 20 career-changers using phone-video screening and a $50 tracker. Log attendance, attrition and minor injuries against the prior cohort. Take the numbers to the contractors' workers' comp broker to negotiate a premium-credit pilot.

title: Per-Class Portable Benefits for Fitness Instructors
one_liner: A payout layer that skims a small per-class contribution from studios and class apps into each 1099 instructor's own injury income protection, health-premium credit and retirement account, structured to give studios legal cover under portable-benefits laws.
customer: Boutique studio groups with 5-30 locations, gym franchisees, class marketplaces and corporate-wellness providers that use 1099 instructors, paying $0.50-2 per class. Instructors opt in for bonus benefits. Trainer associations are a distribution channel.
problem: Several hundred thousand US fitness instructors and trainers work at 3-6 venues, mostly as part-time or self-employed workers with no disability cover, workers' comp or retirement plan. Enhanced ACA subsidies expired in 2026, federal-marketplace enrollment fell about 21%, and an estimated 4.8M people became uninsured, so self-employed instructors' premiums jumped. Injuries to voices, knees and backs end income immediately. Studios face misclassification suits, and because each studio has separate payroll, no one accumulates benefits.
solution: Integrate with scheduling systems (Mindbody, Momence, Walla) to read classes taught. Studios contribute a per-class amount into each instructor's benefits wallet, for example $1.25. The wallet buys short-term income protection through a partner insurer, an ACA premium top-up or HSA deposit, and an IRA contribution. Contributions follow the instructor across venues. The structure is designed to fit safe harbors in states that have passed portable-benefits laws since 2023 (verify current list and get legal review).
why_now: ACA subsidy expiry hit self-employed workers in 2026. A handful of states have passed portable-benefits laws since 2023 that shield platforms from treating contributions as employment evidence. Class-pass economics keep instructors spread across venues. Misclassification exposure keeps studio owners nervous.
revenue_model: A platform fee of 8-10% of contributions, insurer commissions of 12-20% on income protection, and interchange on a benefits card. 10,000 instructors at $2,000 a year in contributions is $20M of flow and about $1.6-2M of revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Portable benefits have struggled with gig platforms because work units are messy. Fitness instructors' work is already itemized in software as class events, so a contribution per class is a natural unit. Fitness is the ideal beachhead because work is high-frequency, discrete, multi-venue and tracked, and instructors are health-literate and physically at risk, so they will value injury protection.
first_30_days: Sign one 10-studio group. Run contributions through a simple ACH from the studio. Partner with an existing accident and disability MGA for a $2-4 a week income-protection policy. Enroll 100 instructors and pilot a $1-per-class contribution. Track instructor retention at the studio and first claims. Target 500 instructors within six months.

title: Keep the 58-Year-Old Machinist Two Years Longer
one_liner: Carrier-co-funded ergonomic and assistive-tech programs that delay retirements instead of chasing new hires.
customer: Manufacturers with 30-300 employees and an older workforce. Workers' comp carriers and brokers co-fund it through loss-control budgets and premium credits.
problem: The industry chases Deloitte and Manufacturing Institute's 3.8M hires needed by 2033, with 1.9M possibly unfilled. Their 2024 report stresses retention, not just applicants. About 60% of manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+. Each retiring senior machinist takes years of tacit skill, and recruiting and training replacements is slow and costly.
solution: A 90-day Longevity Program. It starts with an ergonomic assessment of every role held by workers aged 50+. Then it installs a kit of lift assists, tilting fixtures, better lighting and vibration-damped tool holders, plus optional exoskeleton pilots for overhead work. It also designs phased-retirement roles (for example, mentor three days a week). It tracks injuries and retention against a baseline.
why_now: Manufacturing jobs are up 58k since the December 2025 low, so labor is tightening. Announced reshoring hires land 12-24 months after announcements. Lift-assist and exoskeleton hardware is now cheap enough for small shops.
revenue_model: $8-25k per program plus about $150 per employee per month for monitoring and a training-video library. Finder fees from carriers. Optional performance pricing tied to retention.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest hire is the one who does not retire. Insurers already fund loss control for exactly this age group, so the shop's cost is partly paid by a third party with a matching incentive. My rough estimate is that one avoided senior-machinist retirement is worth well over $100k in replacement, scrap and customer risk.
first_30_days: Call loss-control reps at three regional workers' comp carriers or brokers. Offer three free shop assessments. Document before-and-after injury and absence data. Use the results to sell paid programs to the shops.

title: AI-Label Pre-Flight Before You Upload
one_liner: A 'spellcheck for platform AI labels' that predicts how each service will tag and treat a file before it goes live.
customer: Social video teams, agencies, MCNs, podcast networks, and labels or distributors delivering to several DSPs, all of whom use mixed tool chains.
problem: Every major platform now labels or penalizes AI content: YouTube auto-labels (May 27), TIDAL badges and demonetizes (Jul 15), Snapchat stopped recommending fully-AI Spotlight content (Jul 31), and Spotify excludes AI persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11). Labels can be triggered by markers in any single asset, such as one generative b-roll clip or an AI retouch, and rules differ per platform. Teams cannot predict outcomes.
solution: Upload the final export or stem set. The tool reads C2PA manifests, IPTC DigitalSourceType and XMP, runs public watermark verifiers where they exist, applies per-platform rule tables, and predicts the label and monetization outcome per service. It points to the timeline segments or assets that triggered it, drafts accurate disclosure text, and logs the result. It recommends fixes such as re-rendering a clip, and never strips manifests. Ships as plugins for Premiere, Resolve and Frame.io plus an API for DAM systems.
why_now: Platform penalties for AI labeling only became real between May and Aug 2026, and the rules differ across services. Content Credentials adoption (TikTok joined in Jul 2026) means more assets carry markers.
revenue_model: $49-499/month per team, an API at $0.02 per asset, and $2-10k/month enterprise plans.
non_obvious_insight: The market has focused on creating labels and detecting AI. Once labels carry monetization consequences, the demand is for predicting them, like SEO tools for policy. Honest teams with minor assistive AI, not cheats, are the buyers, and the product keeps disclosure accurate.
first_30_days: Build a parser on the open-source c2pa-rs library plus a rule table from published policies. Test it on 200 real videos. Offer 10 agencies a free label audit of their last 20 uploads and sell the first team plans.

title: Warranty-Linked Installer Certification for African Solar Batteries
one_liner: Battery and inverter brands pay per certified installer and per registered installation, and every certification requires geotagged commissioning proof, which builds an installed-base registry that lenders and insurers cannot otherwise get.
customer: Battery and inverter brands and their distributors in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana (and Indian rooftop and backup-power distributors), paying about $8-15 per registered install plus certification event fees. Asset lenders and insurers pay later for registry data. Installers pay $15-25 for the badge.
problem: Africa has imported more battery dollars than panel dollars from China since 2024, and 75% of solar growth is distributed. Ember estimates its numbers are 2x the official statistics, and only 14 of 54 countries reported 2025 data. Bad installs (loose lugs, undersized cable, misconfigured battery communications) drive warranty costs and fires. Brands cannot tell who installed what and where. Lenders and insurers cannot price the risk.
solution: A 2-day practical certification in a rented workshop with real inverters, batteries and torque tests, run by senior local installers. After certification, every job requires a geotagged photo checklist and serial scans through a WhatsApp or lightweight app flow, and the brand's warranty desk validates instantly. In return installers get faster claims, brand lead flow and pricing power. Trainees come from underemployed electrical-engineering graduates and, reportedly, technicians returning from Gulf jobs.
why_now: Africa is installing about 17 GW in 2026 (+45% year on year), with batteries now the larger import dollar. The Hormuz-linked energy shock and diesel costs push more households and shops toward backup power. India's induction-cooktop rush (reported 20-25x demand) is stressing home wiring and backup systems. Official statistics cannot see any of it, so private registries have unusual value.
revenue_model: $8-15 per registered install from the brand, $1-3k per certification event, and $15-25 badge fees from installers. Lenders and insurers pay $20-60k a year for registry access, or per-lookup fees.
non_obvious_insight: The certification is the data-collection mechanism. Nobody can sell a registry to a lender directly, but every installer will sign up for a badge that speeds warranty claims, and the registry is exhaust from that. It fixes the exact blind spot Ember describes, and the payer at the start is the brand with a warranty bill, not the trainee.
first_30_days: Pick Lagos or Nairobi. Sign one distributor of a top-five battery brand as the pilot payer, using its own warranty-claim cost as the case. Rent a workshop and certify 30-40 installers on day one, with the distributor covering $20 per head. Use WhatsApp plus a form tool with serial-number OCR and no custom code. Target 300 registered installs in 90 days and show the brand the change in its claim rate.

title: Work-From-Abroad Compliance Ledger for Employers
one_liner: A Slack-native ledger that tracks where remote employees actually work and flags tax, payroll, permanent-establishment and visa thresholds before 30 days from Lisbon becomes a liability.
customer: Remote-first companies with 50-1,000 employees, their HR and finance teams, and the tax advisors who serve them.
problem: Over 40 countries have nomad visas with thresholds from under USD 1,000 to over USD 7,000 per month, and some ban local employment. The EU Entry/Exit System has tracked non-EU travellers' 90/180-day stays automatically since April 2026. Employees informally work abroad, and companies do not know their exposure. Consumer trackers show individuals their days but give employers no aggregate view or approval flow.
solution: An opt-in ledger built from calendar entries, flight emails and optional device location, with a rules engine per country (183-day tests, 90/180 rules, permanent-establishment risk days, social-security thresholds, nomad-visa work rules). Employees request a workation, get an auto-check, then a manager approves. Export an evidence pack for tax advisors.
why_now: EES is fully live since April 2026, nomad visas keep multiplying, tax authorities are tightening, and return-to-office fights push employees to work from abroad informally.
revenue_model: USD 4-8 per employee per month with a USD 2K annual minimum, plus advisor referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the employer holding the liability, not the nomad. Information is free (Nomads.com sells lifetime membership for USD 1), so value has moved to compliance evidence and approval workflow.
first_30_days: Interview 20 HR leads at remote startups through remote-first communities. Build a Slack bot that answers '/workation Lisbon 6/1-6/30' with rules for 10 countries. Charge a flat USD 150 per month and partner with 2 international tax firms.

title: Battery Passport Onboarding for E-Bike and Storage Makers
one_liner: Done-for-you EU battery passport, QR labelling and supplier data collection for makers of e-bikes, scooters and industrial or stationary batteries facing the 18 Feb 2027 date.
customer: Mid-size e-bike, e-scooter and light-EV brands, industrial battery pack assemblers and BESS integrators selling in the EU (20-500 staff), plus importers who count as the manufacturer.
problem: The EU Battery Regulation requires from 18 Feb 2027 a QR code and electronic battery passport for EV, light-transport and industrial batteries above 2 kWh (background knowledge; verify current status and any slippage). The data spans composition, cell supplier, recycled content, carbon footprint and state of health, and it must be extracted from cell makers who resist sharing. Larger passport vendors serve automakers and big OEMs, so small assemblers fall through.
solution: A supplier data-collection portal with templates for cell makers, a passport record generator with public and restricted access tiers, QR label files, state-of-health data hooks, a compliance checklist and change updates, plus a service layer that chases suppliers until they answer.
why_now: About 20 weeks remain, delegated acts and standards are still in flux, and small makers cannot wait for perfect specs. Even if parts slip, buyers still need the underlying data.
revenue_model: EUR 8-30k onboarding plus EUR 3-10k/year platform per battery family, with supplier-chasing billed hourly.
non_obvious_insight: The passport is a supplier-data-chasing problem, not a blockchain problem. Small buyers can pool leverage as a buying club so a cell maker answers one questionnaire instead of fifty.
first_30_days: Compile 200 EU e-bike and light-EV brands via a trade body and email a 'passport readiness scorecard'. Sign five design partners at EUR 5k and negotiate a template data sheet with two cell makers.

title: Secret-Shopper Audits of Government Algorithms
one_liner: Submit synthetic applicants and questions to public benefits systems, chatbots and eligibility tools to measure real error and denial rates, then sell the evidence.
customer: State auditors and legislative oversight offices, legal-aid funders, civil-rights litigators, and government AI vendors that want an independent seal before a contract renewal.
problem: State and local buyers cannot audit the AI they bought, and no one owns post-award monitoring. Michigan's fraud detector wrongly accused 40,000 people and cost $20M plus $78M for a replacement. Contracts run 7 years with only 3% of provisions covering cybersecurity.
solution: Run agent-driven synthetic-case testers against public-facing eligibility screeners, 311 and permit chatbots, and (with authorization) internal decision tools. Publish error-rate and disparity reports with reproducible test cases. Offer a continuous monitoring subscription to buyers.
why_now: Cities and counties have moved from pilots to production AI, and the Glass/Sourcewell marketplace pilot covers about 120 agencies. Agentic testers are cheap in 2026, and Michigan makes the harm undeniable.
revenue_model: $30-120K per audit engagement, $5-15K per month for monitoring, and grant-funded public-interest audits. Vendors pay for certified re-tests.
non_obvious_insight: Public-interest audit funders and state auditors already have budgets and mandate but no measurement tool. The synthetic-case method needs no vendor cooperation and no data access.
first_30_days: Run a free audit of 10 public-facing city or state chatbots and publish the findings. Send the report to state auditors and legal-aid funders. Sign one paid audit from a funder or auditor.

title: Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion
one_liner: A completion contractor that takes half-built solar jobs abandoned by bankrupt installers all the way to permission-to-operate, and is paid by the lenders whose loans go bad while the system sits dark.
customer: Solar loan originators and servicers, and TPO sponsors, that now hold stranded projects. The seven finance partners named in the Freedom Forever order are the first buyers: GoodLeap, EnFin, Credit Human, EverBright, Participate, Project Solar and Sunrun. Credit unions and ABS trustees holding 2023-2025 solar loans are the second wave. Homeowners are the beneficiary but do not pay.
problem: When a big installer dies, thousands of systems are left installed but not energized, or half-built. Freedom Forever went Chapter 11 in April 2026 and converted to Chapter 7 on Aug 7, 2026, with about 1,600 layoffs. The borrower stops paying a $30-50k loan on a roof that produces nothing. Lender, homeowner and dead installer each say it is someone else's job. The court let lenders hire new contractors and push systems to PTO, but a lender has no bench of crews and no playbook for doing it.
solution: Run the work as a records-recovery business first and a crew business second. For each stranded job, build a forensic pack: the AHJ permit file, the utility interconnection record, the design set from the dead company's design and CRM tools, equipment serials from distributors and consignment records, and a site photo audit. Sort jobs into tiers: paperwork-only (contractor of record and engineer's stamp need re-issuing), inspection fix, missing hardware, and never started (unwind and refund path). Price each tier at a fixed fee plus a bonus at PTO, and subcontract the labor to licensed local electricians and laid-off installer crews. Give the lender a dashboard of its whole stranded book with cost to cure and expected PTO date.
why_now: Freedom Forever's Chapter 7 conversion (Aug 2026, creditor claims due Oct 16, 2026) and the court order letting financiers step in make this concrete now. Sunnova (June 2025), SunPower (Aug 2024) and 100+ other solar failures came before it. Post-25D volume is down in 2026, so more failures are likely. Lenders have step-in rights but no operating capacity.
revenue_model: Fixed completion fee of $1.5-4k per job by tier, plus a $500 success bonus at PTO, paid by the lender or servicer. Add a monthly stranded-book dashboard subscription. Later, sell a 12-month workmanship warranty on completed jobs, paid by the lender, and a retainer for standby capacity when the next installer fails.
non_obvious_insight: A stranded job is 80% a records and legal-standing problem, not a labor problem. Permits, interconnection applications, engineer stamps and design files sit in a dead contractor's name and portal logins, so nobody can legally finish even though laid-off crews are cheap and plentiful. Also, the buyer is the lender and not the homeowner. The lender's collateral is worthless while the system is dark, it already has contractual step-in rights, and outsiders assume the homeowner is the customer.
first_30_days: Message loss-mitigation and installer-failure leads at 3-4 lenders. Use former installer ops people on LinkedIn to get the introductions. Offer to complete 10 stranded jobs in one metro at cost-plus, with payment on PTO. Recruit 3 laid-off project managers or permit coordinators and 1-2 licensed electrician subs. Write the per-AHJ and per-utility contractor-of-record transfer checklist. Target the first 10 PTOs inside 60 days, with case studies from them.

title: Accessibility Disclosure Kit for US Independent Hotels
one_liner: A phone-based room-measurement kit that produces the accessibility details federal law requires on booking pages, before serial plaintiffs sue.
customer: US independent hotels and small groups of 30-300 rooms, franchisees, and the ADA-defence law firms who refer them.
problem: The federal hotel reservation rule (28 CFR 36.302(e)) requires booking systems to give enough detail about accessible rooms for guests to judge suitability, yet most sites just say 'ADA room'. Serial-filer suits repeat across the same properties and cost thousands each to settle. AI booking assistants also need structured answers on step-free showers and bed heights.
solution: A staff app guides a 20-minute walkthrough per room type using phone measurement and photos (door widths, turning space, shower type, bed height, grab bars). It generates compliant descriptions and a structured feed for OTAs, Google and AI assistants, then monitors listings for drift and provides a litigation-readiness pack.
why_now: Hotels are now being listed in AI assistants that demand structured attributes, and phones with depth sensing make measurement cheap. Serial-filer litigation continues, which gives the wedge and the budget.
revenue_model: USD 600-1,500 one-time per property plus USD 25-60 per month for monitoring, with rev-share to referring law firms.
non_obvious_insight: The lawsuit gets you the budget and the structured data is the moat. Detailed accessibility data is the missing input for agent booking, and accessible travel is an underserved segment.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 ADA-defence firms. Run a free scan showing what a serial filer sees on 100 hotel websites as lead-gen, and sell a USD 499 audit to 20 properties.

title: Pre-Registered Neighbor Impact Studies for Data Centers
one_liner: A neutral 'testing lab' for whether a data center, battery plant or transmission line lowers nearby home values, with the method locked and published before anyone sees the results.
customer: Four payers. (1) Data center, BESS, solar and transmission developers facing moratoria or rezoning hearings pay $15-60k per study. (2) County and city planning departments and utility commissions pay $10-40k for a neutral study. (3) Resident coalitions and HOAs pay $3-8k for a 'lite' study, usually crowdfunded. (4) Landowner condemnation and easement attorneys.
problem: Every land-use fight ends in dueling consultant reports. Developer studies use hand-picked matched pairs that always show 'no impact'. Residents bring anecdotes. Planning staff can't judge either side, so boards vote on vibes and moratoria spread. Nobody trusts any report, so the reports are worthless.
solution: A repeatable, pre-registered protocol. Step 1: publish (timestamped and hashed) the analysis plan, including radius bands, event dates and exclusion rules. Step 2: pull every arm's-length sale within 0.25 to 2 miles, before and after the announcement date and the operation date. Step 3: run a repeat-sales difference-in-differences or synthetic-control analysis against similar areas that had no project. Step 4: have a licensed appraiser review every sale for arm's-length status, condition and segment (estates, REO and investor flips get pulled), and do a ground visit for what is actually audible and visible from the homes. Step 5: deliver a USPAP-compliant consulting report plus an interactive map. Results are published whichever way they come out. Add a 5-year 'impact monitor' subscription for counties and developers that tracks post-operation sales.
why_now: AI-driven data center siting in 2025-26 has produced local moratoria, rezoning denials and noise complaints in many states (VA, GA, TX, AZ, IN, OH). Property values are one of the top arguments alongside power and water. Federal and state pushes to speed up transmission and energy siting mean more condemnation and easement fights. Public sales data plus cheap compute make a rigorous study a $10k job instead of a $100k one.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee studies, paid upfront into escrow so the client cannot steer the result. Annual retainers for repeat developers (for example 8-10 sites a year). $10-15k/yr monitoring subscriptions for counties. Later, an 'Impact Study Standard' certification that planning codes can reference.
non_obvious_insight: Appraisers know matched-pair studies are the hired gun's favorite toy: pick 6 pairs that support the client and you're done, and both sides know it. Credibility is the scarce input, not analysis. Pre-registration is standard in clinical trials and unheard of in appraisal. Developers will pay for a study that might go against them, because a study nobody believes is worth nothing at a hearing. The other secret is timing. Buyer perception moves at announcement, before the first shovel, so studies run only on 'after operation' miss the effect. A difference-in-differences on the announcement date catches it.
first_30_days: Pick one hot metro (for example Northern Virginia or metro Atlanta). Run a free 'shadow study' on existing data centers there using public sales records, with the method pre-registered on a public page. Email planning directors, 10 resident groups and 5 developer permitting leads. Recruit two appraisers as signing reviewers. Aim to sign one $12-20k study, or a county pilot, by day 30-45.

title: Insider-Trading Watchdog for Entertainment Announcements
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for game publishers, studios and awards bodies whose announcements and results now trade as prediction-market contracts.
customer: Legal and compliance teams at game publishers, film and TV studios, awards bodies, esports leagues and streamers. Prediction-market exchanges are a secondary buyer.
problem: Kalshi valuation went from about $11B to $22B between Dec 2025 and May 2026, and entertainment and awards are already about 11% of activity. Employees, agencies, vendors and journalists under embargo hold non-public information that now has a price. No one monitors it, and sports leagues already pay for integrity services that entertainment lacks.
solution: Map every listed contract on Kalshi, Polymarket and other venues to the client's titles, awards and announcements. Detect abnormal volume and price moves ahead of reveals, and deliver incident packets for counsel. Add embargo-tier employee policy and training, and give exchanges a restricted-list API.
why_now: Prediction markets are expanding beyond sports despite state fights, and regulators will demand integrity partners as entertainment contracts multiply.
revenue_model: $2-10k per month subscriptions for IP owners, exchange-side API fees, and forensic investigations at project rates.
non_obvious_insight: Publishers think prediction markets are a gambling issue for someone else. For the first time, their 5,000 employees and 300 vendors hold embargoed information worth money. Sports solved this with third-party integrity vendors, and entertainment has none.
first_30_days: Build a tracker of all entertainment and gaming contracts across major venues. Publish a report on volume spikes before announcements. Contact compliance heads at 10 publishers and awards bodies, and sell one 3-month pilot at $5k per month.

title: TurkBridge: MTurk-Compatible Verified-Human Marketplace
one_liner: An MTurk requester-API-compatible endpoint backed by an identity-verified, proof-of-human worker pool, launched as Amazon Mechanical Turk closes on 30 Sept 2026.
customer: Academic labs and survey researchers, small ML data-labeling teams, and apps that use human-in-the-loop micro-tasks through boto3 or psiTurk-style code. Displaced MTurk workers are the supply side.
problem: Amazon closes MTurk on 30 Sept 2026 and the FAQ names no alternatives or migration path. New HITs end 30 Sept, bonuses are possible until 30 Oct, and transaction history is inaccessible after 28 Jan 2027. SageMaker Ground Truth and Augmented AI lose the MTurk worker type on the same date. Requesters have legacy code and no drop-in replacement, and quality was already collapsing because workers submitted AI output. One HN user says their app 'has been using Amazon Mechanical Turk for left-pad queries, and that service is shutting down in less than two weeks.'
solution: (1) Publish an API shim that mimics the MTurk requester operations (CreateHIT, ListAssignmentsForHIT, ApproveAssignment, qualification requirements, sandbox), so a codebase migrates by changing an endpoint URL. (2) Build supply from ex-MTurk workers on Turkopticon and worker forums, who lose income on the closure date. Give each worker a verified unique-person identity, passkey and liveness checks, and behavioural anti-LLM signals. (3) Sell two tiers, 'verified human' and 'domain expert', with paid-per-task quality gates. The product is the proof that a human did the work, priced above the old race-to-the-bottom rate.
why_now: The shutdown date is two days away, and worker income disappears the same day. Generic open crowd platforms have been wrecked by LLMs, so verified humanness has become the scarce good. Identity-verification APIs are now cheap (Didit, 'Stripe for Identity Verification', launched on HN in March 2026).
revenue_model: A 20-30% take on task payments, a $99/mo lab plan with participant-screening tools, and a per-verification fee for enterprise annotation buyers.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is trust in who is doing the task, and the API compatibility is what lets you take the customers. The MTurk FAQ confirms the dates and lists no alternative or migration path (https://www.mturk.com/help). In the 534-point HN thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49457545), dubeye writes: 'The problem as I see it is verifying the work is not done by AI. If it was possible to verify somehow that the work is definitely not done by AI I think there would still be a market.' Another user found MNIST accuracy from Ground Truth on MTurk 'marginally better than guessing.' Prolific is named as the maintained alternative, but I found no evidence that any alternative offers MTurk API compatibility. Legacy scripts are the switching cost, and the shim removes it.
first_30_days: Week 1: write the shim covering the 6 most-used MTurk operations, using boto3's endpoint_url override. Post a 'migrate in 10 minutes' guide on r/mturk, psiTurk and academic Twitter. Weeks 2-3: onboard the first 300-500 workers with ID and liveness checks. Recruit 5 lab requesters with free credits in exchange for case studies. Week 4: run paid studies, publish a proof-of-human quality comparison against raw MTurk data, and start charging the take rate.

title: Stablecoin Cash-Out Float for Corner Shops
one_liner: Stablecoins made sending money nearly free, so the scarce thing is cash at the last mile, and the margin goes to whoever finances the agents.
customer: Pharmacies, tiendas and kiosks that act as cash-out agents in Colombia, Mexico, Argentina and Nigeria, plus the stablecoin remittance and wallet apps that need them.
problem: A $200 US-to-Colombia transfer costs $12.13 on legacy rails versus about $0.01 in stablecoins, but recipients still want local cash. Small agents run out of float and refuse large withdrawals.
solution: A float-management app that shows each agent's cash position, advances intraday float against next-day USDC settlement and routes recipients to agents with liquidity. The wedge is 100 pharmacies on one remittance corridor for a single anchor partner.
why_now: Nigeria opened a stablecoin sandbox (Aug 12) and Kenya passed digital-currency legislation (Aug 6). Yellow Card is hiring in LatAm and SEA, and Felix has processed $8B over WhatsApp.
revenue_model: A 1-1.5% spread on float turnover plus a per-payout fee from the remitter.
non_obvious_insight: As stablecoin transfer fees go to zero, the margin migrates to the last ten metres of physical cash. This is cash logistics dressed up as fintech.
first_30_days: Sign one wallet or remittance partner as anchor and raise a roughly $50k float line from a debt fund. Onboard 20 pharmacies in one city.

title: A Price Index and Exchange for Agent Labor
one_liner: Publish the going rate and accuracy for standardized agent-delivered tasks (per 1,000 invoices, per verified ticket resolution), then let buyers run reverse auctions against it.
customer: CFOs, procurement and ops leaders at enterprises buying agent services, investors and analysts, and later the agent vendors that bid for work.
problem: Buyers have no reference price. Vendor pricing is opaque and shifting from seats to outcomes, quality varies widely, and Gartner says only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic' vendors are real. Unit token prices fell about 67% but bills rose, so nobody knows what a task should cost.
solution: Define standardized task classes with public test sets and acceptance criteria (invoice extraction and coding, tier-1 support resolution, KYC document review, meeting scheduling). Run blinded monthly bake-offs across vendors on hidden holdouts and publish a quality and cost-per-verified-outcome index. Sell buyer-side bake-offs on customers' own data. Later add an RFQ exchange with escrow released when acceptance tests pass.
why_now: Outcome pricing arrived in 2026, agent-washing is rampant, and benchmarks exist for models but not end-to-end vendors. Project Vend-style real-world evaluations show that outcomes need checklists and supervision to be trustworthy.
revenue_model: $20-$60k/year subscriptions for enterprises and investors, $15-$40k custom bake-offs, and a 3-5% exchange take rate later.
non_obvious_insight: Markets need a benchmark price before they need a marketplace, as freight and housing indices came first. Agent labor has large quality and price dispersion, and the party that publishes the reference sets the negotiation frame for the whole category.
first_30_days: Pick 2 task classes and assemble public plus holdout data. Run 6 vendors and publish the first index free with full methodology. Sell the first custom bake-off to a buyer and use it as a case study.

title: Standby Mass-Fatality Cooler Network for Counties
one_liner: A retainer-based network of vetted funeral homes with cooler space, vans and chain-of-custody training that counties and hospital coalitions can activate when the morgue overflows.
customer: County emergency managers, medical examiner and coroner offices, regional Health Care Coalitions and hospital systems. They fund it through preparedness grants, state emergency-management budgets and hospital readiness budgets.
problem: Mass-fatality plans routinely say 'coordinate with local funeral directors', which is a handshake with no contract, no capacity inventory, no shared identification protocol and no payment. ME planning guides size storage at roughly 1.5x average daily caseload plus a 25% surge buffer, so a heat wave, hurricane, flood or outbreak blows through it. Counties then scramble for refrigerated trailers, which are undignified, poorly tracked, and a magnet for misidentification scandals. Funeral homes are willing to help but can't say what they can commit and dread not being paid.
solution: Enroll 10-30 funeral homes per region. Run a capacity survey (cooler slots, bariatric capability, generators, on-call staff, vehicles). Train them in ID and chain-of-custody basics, personal-effects logging and family-notification etiquette, a DMORT-lite curriculum. Credential their licenses and insurance. Provide a shared dashboard and case-tracking app with unique IDs, tags, photos and effects logs that exports to the ME's systems. Sell the county or coalition a one-to-three-year readiness retainer with an annual tabletop exercise and pre-negotiated per-diem activation rates. Add an 'everyday overflow' service for ME backlogs, such as holiday weekends and opioid or heat spikes, at per-case rates, which turns readiness into recurring revenue.
why_now: Federal disaster support is being pushed toward states and counties, so local preparedness is becoming a locally funded line item. Record heat deaths in the Southwest and busy hurricane seasons keep overloading morgues. ME offices are visibly overflowing, and new facilities such as Jacksonville's in 2026 are being built with triple capacity. Forensic pathologist shortages slow releases and keep bodies in coolers longer.
revenue_model: Annual readiness retainer of $15,000-$60,000 per county or coalition region, with a stipend of about $3,000-$8,000 flowing to each participating funeral home. Activation per diem of $75-$150 per body per day. Overflow per-case fees. $8,000-$15,000 for tabletop exercises and training. Software license for the tracking app.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset in a mass-fatality event isn't refrigerated trucks, it's trusted, licensed humans with cooled rooms already in every zip code, and they sit about 70% idle. No one has ever paid funeral homes to stay ready. Public trust collapses over identification and chain-of-custody errors, not storage, and funeral directors are the only civilians who do that work every day.
first_30_days: Pick one heat- and hurricane-exposed region. Recruit 10-15 funeral homes through the state funeral directors' association. Write a 12-page letter-of-commitment and capacity template. Book meetings with five county emergency managers and two Health Care Coalition coordinators (public directories). Offer a $7,500 paid tabletop exercise plus regional capacity map, priced under many small-purchase thresholds. Convert the exercise participants to a retainer proposal.

title: Overtourism Feed for AI Travel Agents
one_liner: A destination-signed, machine-readable feed of live capacity, closures and dispersal incentives that AI trip agents query, so places can steer planning before tourists arrive.
customer: Destination management organisations and city tourism boards in overtouristed regions (Balearics, Dolomites, Kyoto, Lisbon, Dubrovnik, Amsterdam), later transport agencies and hotel groups.
problem: AI agents now plan and book trips (Booking.com and Expedia apps run inside ChatGPT), and they recommend the same hotspots blind to caps, closures and crowding. DMOs intervene only after arrival with fees and fines, which Venice's reportedly ineffective day-tripper fee shows is weak. Referral traffic from search is being eaten by AI answers.
solution: Publish an MCP server and JSON feed per destination with a daily load index by place and hour (from ticketing, parking, cruise calendars and occupancy), hard caps and permits, equivalent alternatives within about 60 minutes with partner lodging, resident-first hours and off-peak incentive codes. DMOs get a dashboard showing how many agent-planned trips shifted. Start with a hosted API and a DMO-embedded chatbot for immediate use.
why_now: OTA apps are now inside AI assistants, MCP servers are mainstream, booking lead times are shrinking, and AI overviews reportedly cut metasearch clicks by 31% in tested markets. DMOs need a way to influence the plan rather than the queue.
revenue_model: DMO subscriptions of EUR 20-100K per year, transparent sponsored 'dispersal' placements paid by under-visited partners, and analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism control is an information-timing problem. Influence must happen at itinerary generation, and AI agents are the first chokepoint where a single feed can shape millions of itineraries, giving destinations robots.txt-style power.
first_30_days: Build a feed for one region from public data (cruise schedules, park permit status, museum time slots) and ship the MCP server. Offer 3 DMOs a free traffic dashboard as design partners and embed it in their own website chatbots. Approach trip-planner app builders for consumption.

title: Muthoot-Style Gold Loans for America's Junk Drawers
one_liner: A mail-in, XRF-assayed loan against gold and jewelry at roughly 24-36% APR, versus 200%-plus at a typical US pawn shop, run through licensed pawn partners for people who need $300-$5,000 and have idle gold worth far more with gold trading around $4,100-$4,500 an ounce.
customer: Middle-income households aged 35-65 with jewelry and coins in a drawer and thin or damaged credit who need a few hundred to a few thousand dollars for a car repair, rent gap or tax bill. Small-business owners with a cash-flow gap are the second segment.
problem: Cash-for-gold buyers pay a fraction of melt value with no way to get the piece back. Pawn shops charge 10-25% a month. Payday and title lenders charge triple-digit APRs. The only cheap collateral-backed product is stigmatized, store-based and priced for rent rather than risk, so many people with real assets choose worse options or sell irreplaceable pieces at a loss.
solution: Mail an insured kit (or drop off at a partner pawn store). On receipt, run an XRF assay and weigh, then offer 70-75% of melt value within hours and pay by ACH. Redeem by paying principal plus interest, and the piece comes back insured. If the borrower does not repay, the gold is sold at melt with any surplus returned where state law requires. There is no collections calling and no credit reporting. Interest is about 2% a month falling for repeat borrowers. Hedge the collateral pool with gold futures. Launch through a licensed pawnbroker as lender of record, then license state by state.
why_now: Gold has traded roughly between $4,100 and $4,500 an ounce in September 2026, so a drawer of old 14k jewelry is worth several times what it was in 2022. Indian gold-loan lenders (Muthoot, Rupeek and others) have shown that 9-25% APR gold lending is profitable at scale, while US pawn remains a fragmented, store-based, high-rate market. Cheap XRF analyzers, insured shipping and instant ACH remove the storefront cost that justified those US rates.
revenue_model: Interest of 1.5-2.5% a month on outstanding loans, plus a small handling fee on loans under $500, plus surplus on forfeited gold sold above the loan amount. Funded by a private-credit warehouse line at low double-digit cost of capital. Because loans are 70-75% of a liquid commodity's melt value, credit losses are close to hedging and shipping costs.
non_obvious_insight: The 200%-plus APR of US pawn is not a price for risk, because collateral makes the loss very small. It is a price for store rent, low volume and stigma. Remove the storefront and the mass-market stigma (customers are gold owners with poor liquidity, not desperate borrowers) and you can undercut incumbents 5-8x on price and still earn better returns on capital than a bank.
first_30_days: Sign a licensed pawnbroker in Texas or Florida as lender of record so you inherit their license and compliance, including police reporting of transactions. Buy an XRF analyzer and a rated insured vault or use a custody partner. Raise about $250k to fund the first 50-100 loans. Buy search and social ads that intercept 'sell my gold' intent and publish the true APR up front. First loans should close within 4-6 weeks, and the pilot's default and hedging data becomes the pitch for a credit line.

title: GPS Spoofing Alarm Using LEO Signals
one_liner: A passive receiver that listens to Starlink, OneWeb and Iridium-style signals and flags when GPS disagrees.
customer: Shipping companies and port authorities in jammed regions (Baltic, Persian Gulf, Red Sea), aviation operators, telecom timing operators, drone fleets, and hull and P&I insurers.
problem: GNSS jamming and spoofing have spread across shipping and aviation (prior knowledge, 2024-25). Most detection depends on GNSS itself or expensive inertial systems. Operators and insurers want independent evidence of position integrity.
solution: A small software-defined receiver that measures Doppler and timing from LEO communication signals of opportunity and, using public orbit data, checks position and time consistency. First product is an integrity alarm, not a navigator. Later add tens-of-meters holdover navigation.
why_now: There are about 10,000 Starlinks plus other constellations, so signals of opportunity are abundant. Academic demonstrations of positioning from them have matured. Jamming has moved from a defense concern to a commercial one.
revenue_model: $2-5k per unit plus $100 per month cloud analytics. Insurer-funded fleet programs. Government pilots.
non_obvious_insight: You do not need to navigate better than GPS to be valuable, only to disagree with it reliably. Integrity is a cheaper, faster product than replacement navigation.
first_30_days: Build a lab proof of concept using a Ku-band LNB and an SDR. Recruit two Baltic or Gulf ship managers or port operators for field trials. Approach one marine insurer about premium credits for verified integrity.

title: Hyperspectral Target Packs for Natural Hydrogen Explorers
one_liner: Use newly open hyperspectral satellite data to rank licence blocks for natural hydrogen, then sell the evidence pack that helps cash-poor explorers raise money and keep their licences.
customer: Junior explorers and startups holding or applying for natural-hydrogen licences (ASX/TSXV juniors, private startups, landmen leasing in the US Midcontinent, Spain, France, South Australia and the Philippines), plus government surveys running tenders.
problem: Licences and leases are being granted essentially blind in a land rush. Drilling costs millions, and the only surface clues are ultramafic and iron-rich rock, vegetation anomalies and circular depressions. Small explorers cannot afford a full geophysics programme yet need credible evidence for investors and regulators.
solution: A multi-sensor prospectivity pack: hyperspectral mineral mapping (EMIT, Planet Tanager open data, Pixxel tasking) for serpentinized ultramafic rocks and iron-oxide and clay alteration; multi-year vegetation-stress anomalies; Sentinel-2 and SAR detection of circular depressions; then public gravity/magnetics and geology. Output is a ranked block list and a 20-page evidence deck, with an optional partner ground-truth soil-gas hydrogen survey.
why_now: Koloma has raised about $400M and won the first competitive natural-hydrogen bid round in the Philippines (three contracts, over 4,000 km2). A USGS map, DOE grants, EU funding (Mantle 8) and Australian co-funding are all live. Open hyperspectral archives (EMIT, Tanager) and cheap commercial tasking (Pixxel Firefly, about $8/km2 quoted) did not exist three years ago.
revenue_model: $10k to $40k per licence-block pack. $3k to $8k a month monitoring retainer. For cash-poor juniors, part-payment via a small royalty or option in place of cash.
non_obvious_insight: In a gold rush, the scarce product is a credible map that makes the pitch deck and licence renewal defensible, and hyperspectral is unusually good at the specific rock chemistry of serpentinization. You sell ranking plus a ground-truth feedback loop, not certainty, and each drill or soil-gas result improves the model in a way competitors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Back-test on known hydrogen occurrences and known fairy-circle areas to measure hit rate. Publish a free prospectivity map of one region (Kansas/Nebraska Midcontinent Rift or South Australia) to attract leads. Sell three packs to ASX or TSXV juniors at $10k to $15k.

title: Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders
one_liner: Independent-engineer-style diligence and monthly monitoring on the part of a data center build that satellites cannot see: the last 90 days before ready-for-service.
customer: Private credit funds, banks and ABS investors lending against GPUs and neocloud contracts; insurers underwriting delay risk; AI labs and enterprises signing take-or-pay capacity who need to know if the promised RFS date is credible.
problem: GPU-backed loans and offtake contracts are priced on a ready-for-service date. Satellite vendors (SynMax and Industrial Info Resources now cover 2,600+ projects weekly) can show steel, cooling towers and generator yards, but they cannot see the failure zone: utility permission to energize, MV switchgear energization, Level 4/5 commissioning and IST results, liquid-cooling flush and pressure tests, fiber-plant acceptance, OEM startup-tech availability. Percent complete on pay applications is front-loaded and misleading. Meanwhile GPUs costing millions per rack sit idle and depreciate while interest accrues, and lenders are capping neocloud exposure. Traditional IEs are power-plant-oriented, slow and expensive.
solution: A 'Readiness Ladder' of about 40 binary, evidence-backed milestones (utility energization letter, gear serials and bills of lading, Cx level sign-offs, IST pass/fail counts, CDU flush logs, open-punch burn-down rate, OEM startup-tech calendar). Score each project and re-score monthly. Output a probability of RFS by date and covenant or draw-release triggers. Staff it with a bench of ex-data-center PMs and Cx leads who do desk review plus quick site visits. Sell as a 2-week second-opinion product first, then monthly monitoring, integrating vendor satellite feeds as an input rather than competing with them.
why_now: Neocloud credit risk is now the topic. Lenders are capping exposure, deals are stalling on credit risk, and GPU-debt structures (including vendor backstops) are proliferating. Analyses show roughly 40% of AI data center sites with possible delays and about half of 2026 capacity slipping, while operators publicly deny it. Satellite monitoring has commoditized the exterior, which makes the interior truth the scarce and valuable part.
revenue_model: $25K fixed-fee 2-week second opinions; $40K-120K full pre-close diligence; $8K-20K/month per facility monitoring; optional success-based fee for delay-risk insurance placement. Adjacent product: retained RFS-credibility scoring for AI labs choosing between capacity offers.
non_obvious_insight: Percent complete is the wrong metric. The last 5% of a data center can consume 25% of the calendar, and it is dominated by unbounded tasks: the commissioning punch-list burn-down rate and whether the OEM has a startup technician free that month predict RFS far better than construction progress. You can only read those signals if you have run an IST. Also, the RFS date on a marketing sheet is a sales number, not a schedule.
first_30_days: Recruit 6 retired or between-jobs Cx leads and PMs on 1099 contracts. Publish a free 'RFS credibility checklist' and a teardown of one publicly delayed project. Approach 5-10 private credit and infrastructure funds with data center or GPU-lending desks. Offer a fixed-fee $25K second opinion on one live deal, delivered in two weeks, and ask permission to reference the engagement anonymously.

title: Bench-Truth Diligence for Biotech Investors
one_liner: Sell seed VCs, pharma BD teams and AI-bio founders confidential 'does this paper's key result actually work?' intelligence, from anonymous postdoc consensus polls up to paid replication of the one key experiment.
customer: Seed and Series A biotech VCs, corporate venture arms, pharma BD and scouting teams evaluating academic spinouts or in-licensing, and AI-bio startups building on published wet-lab claims. Pay $4-6k for a poll-only memo and $15-40k for a key-experiment replication.
problem: Investors and BD teams can't tell which high-profile papers replicate. The truth exists as hallway consensus: 'that result only works in the first author's hands', 'nobody outside that lab can get the organoid protocol to run', 'cells were cultured as previously described' with four layers of citations. Formal diligence hires KOL consultants who are conflicted and often the PI's friends, or a CRO that needs 4 months and a full protocol. Bad academic-asset bets burn $5-20M before anyone notices.
solution: Wedge product 'Bench Pulse': in 5 business days, poll 8-15 vetted, paid, anonymous postdocs and senior techs working in the exact subfield about the named claim, reagents and protocol. Deliver a structured memo with consensus, red flags, the Figure-3 problem, which reagents or lots are fragile, and a 'what to test first' plan. Upsell: 'Key-Figure Replication'. A pool of laid-off or between-position scientists runs the single decisive experiment in 3-4 weeks in rented bench space (not on university property), with pre-registered success criteria and blinded readout.
why_now: Biotech funding since 2023 rewards capital efficiency, so seed funds want cheaper, faster kill decisions. Pharma is shopping for early assets in academia and abroad. AI-bio companies are building on published wet-lab claims with little bench sense. NIH disruption and biotech layoffs have released a large pool of very good bench scientists who want paid, flexible work. Expert-network compliance norms are now well understood, so a compliant structure is feasible.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee per poll memo and per replication study. Annual retainer for funds that want a pipeline-wide 'bench pulse' (about $30-60k). Optional success-fee or advisory equity for AI-bio startups.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not lab capacity, it is candid consensus. Replication is expensive, but the postdoc informal network already knows which labs' results hold up. The winning move is to monetize that gossip compliantly and only spend on replication after the poll narrows the question. GLG-style expert calls fail because they interview one conflicted senior person instead of 10 juniors who actually do the pipetting.
first_30_days: Choose one subfield you personally have 20 contacts in (for example CAR-T, organoids, targeted protein degradation or spatial biology). Build the compliant NDA plus anonymity protocol with a lawyer for about $3k. Offer 3 seed funds a free poll on one asset they are already looking at. Convert the fund that reacts to a paid $5k poll, then upsell one replication. Pay panelists $150-300 per poll from the first revenue.

title: Retiring Masters' Exit Interviews, Funded by Employers and AI Labs
one_liner: Capture the last generation of unrecorded tradespeople as expert playbooks for their employer and consented, royalty-bearing training data for robotics and industrial-AI labs.
customer: Two payers. Operations and HR leaders at municipal water and wastewater utilities, electric co-ops, machine shops and food plants pay $6-15k per retiring expert. Robotics and maintenance-copilot companies pay to license consented expert demonstration data.
problem: Decades of tacit knowledge walk out the door with baby-boomer retirees: why a pump sounds wrong, how to set up a difficult mold, what to check third when the obvious fixes fail. Written SOPs miss it. Robotics labs can buy cheap novice chore video but have almost no expert-grade manipulation and diagnostic-reasoning data, and crowd-sourced gig filming is hitting a quality ceiling.
solution: A two-person crew, or a mailed camera kit plus a remote interviewer, spends 2-3 days per expert: head-mounted and wrist cameras during real tasks, think-aloud narration, 'what would you check next?' probing, and staged edge cases. Deliverables: (1) an employer-owned playbook of video-indexed SOPs, fault libraries and decision trees, plus a searchable Q&A bot; (2) a de-identified dataset licensed to AI and robotics buyers. The expert gets a retention bonus and a royalty share, and the employer gets a discount in exchange for licensing rights.
why_now: The physical-AI and humanoid boom created a 2025-26 scramble for demonstration data, and large labs and gig apps now pay people to film chores. Chore data saturates quickly, so experts are the next scarce input. The skilled-trades retirement wave is peaking. Maintenance and diagnosis copilots need reasoning traces, not just video.
revenue_model: Employer capture fee of $6-15k per expert; dataset licensing at roughly $100-500 per hour of expert footage with recurring buyers; a follow-on 'build your maintenance copilot' project; royalty pass-through to experts as the trust mechanism.
non_obvious_insight: The highest-value physical-AI data is not being crowd-sourced. It sits in the heads and hands of people who were never recorded, and their employers will pay to capture it for their own continuity reasons. That makes the training data a subsidized by-product, undercutting gig-data vendors on cost and beating them on quality. Royalty-sharing with the expert defuses the consent and labor fight that will otherwise hit the data industry.
first_30_days: Choose one vertical, either municipal wastewater operators or CNC machinists. Recruit 5 soon-to-retire experts through state rural-water associations or machining trade newsletters. Run two paid pilots at a $2.5k intro price with a $400 camera kit. Cut a 20-hour sample reel and send it to 10 robotics and industrial-AI startups to collect letters of intent.
